title: Vectors, matrices, and the dot product
summary: You can read any score function as a dot product, and check its shapes mechanically.

title: Slope → gradient
summary: You can compute a gradient and explain why training steps against it.

title: Probability, expectation, likelihood
summary: You can explain why a loss is a negative log-likelihood, and read mean and variance off a distribution.

title: Supervised learning as function fitting
summary: You can write down (X, y, f_θ, L) for any supervised task and say what is being learned.

title: Generalization: overfitting, underfitting, and the gap
summary: You can diagnose over- vs underfitting from train/test curves and pick the fix that matches the diagnosis.

title: Linear & logistic regression
summary: You can derive a logistic decision boundary, and say why squared error is the wrong loss for classification.

title: Trees & ensembles
summary: You can explain axis-aligned splits, bagging vs boosting, and when trees beat linear models.

title: The neuron: weighted sum plus one bend
summary: You can prove that stacked linear layers collapse into one, so a nonlinearity is mandatory.

title: Layers and the forward pass
summary: You can trace shapes and values through a two-layer network by hand.

title: Backpropagation
summary: You can apply the chain rule to a small graph and say what each gradient means.

title: The training loop
summary: You can write the five-line loop and read a loss curve well enough to diagnose it.

title: Overfitting in deep learning
summary: You can choose among dropout, weight decay, augmentation and early stopping for a given symptom.

title: Optimization failure modes
summary: You can diagnose vanishing or exploding gradients and name the fix.

title: Architecture families: what each one assumes
summary: You can state what MLP, CNN and RNN each assume about data, and choose one for a task.

title: Tokenization: text → integers
summary: You can explain vocabularies, subwords, OOV, and why token count is not word count.

title: Embeddings: meaning as a vector
summary: You can explain the distributional hypothesis and compute cosine similarity.

title: RNN → LSTM: memory that survives
summary: You can explain the fixed-vector bottleneck and how gates address it.

title: Seq2seq & encoder–decoder
summary: You can explain translation as encode-then-decode, and state the alignment problem attention solves.

title: The RL frame: states, actions, rewards
summary: You can formalize a task as (S, A, P, R, γ) and compute a return.

title: Value functions & the Bellman equation
summary: You can write V and Q and explain the recursive expectation.

title: Exploration vs exploitation
summary: You can run ε-greedy by hand and explain regret on a bandit.

title: Two solution families: value vs policy
summary: You can contrast Q-learning and policy gradient on what they learn and when each fails.

title: Function approximation: why tables die
summary: You can explain why tabular RL fails at scale, and why approximation removes the convergence guarantee.

title: DQN: two fixes that made it work
summary: You can explain replay buffer and target network as fixes for correlated data and moving targets.

title: Policy gradient at scale: REINFORCE → PPO
summary: You can trace REINFORCE → baseline → actor–critic → PPO and explain the variance problem.

title: Attention: a soft lookup
summary: You can compute scaled dot-product attention by hand for two tokens and explain the Q/K/V roles.

title: The Transformer block
summary: You can name every sub-layer, its purpose, and why residual + LayerNorm are required.

title: Pretraining: prediction as supervision
summary: You can contrast next-token and masked objectives, and explain what scale buys.

title: Alignment & inference
summary: You can explain SFT → RLHF/DPO, and how context window and temperature shape output.

title: Why explainability exists
summary: You can distinguish intrinsic vs post-hoc and local vs global, and name the accountability use case.

title: Attribution methods: what each one computes
summary: You can explain what saliency, LIME and SHAP compute, and their failure modes.

title: Evaluating explanations
summary: You can test faithfulness and explain the correlation ≠ causation trap.

title: Federated learning & FedAvg
summary: You can describe the round protocol, write the averaging rule, and justify data locality.

title: Non-IID data & client drift
summary: You can explain client drift, name the fixes, and state the local-steps trade-off.

title: Privacy & threat model
summary: You can explain DP noise, secure aggregation, and poisoning/backdoor attacks.

title: Eigenvalues, eigenvectors & SVD
summary: You can find the directions a matrix only stretches, read the stretch factors, and use the SVD to compress or summarise a matrix.

title: Norms & distances
summary: You can compute L1, L2 and max distances on real numbers, explain what each one measures, and say when standardising features changes the answer.

title: Distributions & sampling
summary: You can compute a standard error, read a confidence interval, and say how much a mean would move if the data were collected again.

title: Estimation & bias–variance
summary: You can split an estimator's expected error into bias squared plus variance, and choose between two estimators on that total.

title: kNN & the curse of dimensionality
summary: You can run k-nearest-neighbours by hand, choose k, and explain why adding features can make neighbours meaningless.

title: SVM & kernels

title: Clustering: k-means & GMM
summary: You can run k-means by hand, say what it optimises, and explain when a Gaussian mixture is the better model.

title: PCA & dimensionality reduction
summary: You can centre a matrix, read a covariance, and explain what a principal component's eigenvalue measures.

title: Feature engineering, leakage & imbalance
summary: You can name the moment a feature becomes available, spot leakage in a pipeline, and choose a metric that survives a 2% positive rate.

title: Convolutions & CNNs
summary: You can compute a convolution by hand, size its output, and count its parameters without counting pixels.

title: Initialization & normalization
summary: You can pick a weight initialization, say what variance it preserves, and explain what normalization fixes.

title: Optimizers: SGD → Adam

summary: You can turn logits into a token with greedy, top-k, top-p and temperature, and say what each knob does.

summary: You can compute one attention head, say what multiple heads buy, and explain how position enters the model.

summary: You can compute perplexity and a benchmark's error bar, and say what each one does not measure.

summary: You can write an MDP's five parts and run value iteration on a three-state chain by hand.

summary: You can measure expected calibration error and explain what temperature scaling fixes and what it leaves alone.

summary: You can compute an INT8 scale, bound its rounding error, and explain what a distilled student learns from soft targets.

summary: You can compute a two-sample KS statistic, separate a data-quality break from real drift, and choose a monitoring response.

title: η (eta) — how far one step goes
summary: η sets how much of the slope each step obeys — and decides whether the loss reaches the bottom.

title: Why the update subtracts
summary: The gradient points uphill, so training subtracts it. The minus is a direction, and the gradient's sign decides which way the weights move.

title: −log p — the price of surprise
summary: A model's loss is the surprise of the answer it gave little probability to: −log p, flat near 1 and steep near 0.

title: Σ (sigma) — summing surprise over the data
summary: NLL adds one −log p per row, then divides by the row count so two datasets can be compared.

title: θ (theta) — the numbers that move
summary: Separate the numbers a model learns from the data it is given, using a straight line through three fixed points.

title: f_θ(xᵢ) (theta) — one prediction
summary: Read f-theta of x-i correctly: the model with weights theta applied to one fixed row, producing one number.

title: L(·,·) — the price of being wrong
summary: Compute squared error for one prediction and see why the square matters.

title: L(f_θ(xᵢ) (theta), yᵢ) — the atom
summary: Turn one row into one loss in two steps: predict first, then price the prediction.

title: Σi(sigma) — add the atoms
summary: Read Σᵢ as a running total over examples, and see why the order of the losses does not change the sum.

title: 1/n — turn a total into a rate
summary: Why the objective divides by the number of examples: totals grow with dataset size, rates do not.

title: argmin vs min
summary: Argmin returns the parameter that minimises the loss, not the minimum value.

title: θ* (theta) — optimal for what?
summary: θ* is the best fit for one dataset and one loss — not the true parameters of the world.

title: The whole objective
summary: Read the complete training objective left to right and see it as a landscape.

title: Bias², variance, noise — the three parts of a miss
summary: Split expected error into bias squared, variance and noise, and see which part more data can shrink.

title: σ(z) (sigma) — from score to probability
summary: Read z as a log-odds, push it through the sigmoid, and find the logistic decision boundary.

title: Gini impurity — scoring a split
summary: Compute Gini impurity for a node and for a split, and see why a useless cut leaves it unchanged.

title: Why φ (phi) cannot be removed
summary: Two layers without a bend are one matrix. Multiply W2 by W1 and watch depth buy nothing.

title: Shape algebra — the inner dimensions must meet
summary: Name every shape in a two-layer forward pass and use the inner-dimension rule to predict the output.

title: The chain rule — one slope at a time
summary: Walk one gradient from loss to weight, multiplying the local slopes, and read what the sign means.

title: Fan-out — gradients add, they do not compete
summary: When one value feeds two branches, the backward pass adds their gradients instead of choosing between them.

title: Steps, batches, epochs — three words, one division
summary: Turn a dataset and a batch size into a count of weight updates, and see why epochs alone say nothing.

title: gL — how much gradient survives
summary: Compute how a gradient shrinks or explodes across L layers, and name the fix for each direction.

title: k²·Cin·Cout — where convolution parameters come from
summary: Count the weights in a convolution from its filter size and channels, and see why sharing makes it thousands of times smaller than a dense layer.

title: BPE — merge the most frequent pair
summary: Run four BPE merges by hand and see why token count is not word count.

title: h_t — one state, rewritten
summary: Read the RNN recurrence symbol by symbol and see why a fixed-width state loses the past.

title: f, i, o — the gates
summary: Read the LSTM cell update, compute one step, and see why addition protects the gradient.

title: p(y|x) — the chain rule
summary: Multiply per-token probabilities into one sequence probability, and see what teacher forcing hides.

title: γ (gamma) — the price of waiting
summary: γ shrinks a reward once more for every step of delay, and γ = 0 makes an agent myopic.

title: 1/(1−γ) (gamma) — how far the agent looks
summary: The effective horizon 1/(1−γ) counts the steps a discount still pays attention to.

title: V(s) = r + γV(s′) (gamma) — bootstrapping
summary: Bootstrapping writes a state's value as its reward plus the discounted value of the next state.

title: max — the value of the best action
summary: A maximum over actions turns action values into a state value and a policy.

title: UCB — the optimism bonus
summary: UCB adds a bonus that shrinks with the number of pulls, so untried actions get tried.

title: TD error — target minus estimate
summary: A TD update moves the current estimate a fraction α of the way toward the target r + γ max Q′.

title: r + γ (gamma) max Q(s′,a′) — the frozen answer key
summary: Compute a Q-learning target with frozen weights and explain why the target network stabilises training.

title: r — the ratio, clipped to 1 ± 0.2
summary: Compute PPO's probability ratio and clipped objective, and say what the clip does and does not guarantee.

title: softmax — scores into weights
summary: Turn raw attention scores into weights that are positive and sum to one, by hand, for two and three tokens.

title: 1/√dk(square root) — keeping scores in range
summary: Why attention scores are divided by the square root of the head width, and what saturation costs.

title: x + MHA(LN(x)) — the residual path
summary: Read x plus MHA of LN of x: what the residual copy carries, and why the added identity keeps gradients alive.

title: softmax(z/T) — temperature
summary: Divide logits by a temperature before softmax: one dial, three distributions, no change in ranking.

title: φ (phi) — a fair share of the prediction
summary: Compute the Shapley value for two features by averaging their marginal gain over both orderings.

title: w ← Σ (nₖ/N) (sigma) wₖ — the weighted average
summary: Weight three client models by their example counts and see why FedAvg gives 0.74 rather than 0.50.

title: ε (epsilon) and δ — the shape of a privacy promise
summary: Read a differential privacy guarantee, set clipping and noise, and price the accuracy it costs.
